II-II q.47 a.8.text: [three acts of practical reason:] to take counsel ... to judge of what one has discovered ... to command ... [command] approaches nearer to the end of the practical reason ... the chief act of the practical reason, and consequently of prudence.
II-II q.47 a.8.notes: Fragments as returned by the fetch; a.2 gives 'right reason applied to action' (recta ratio agibilium). Ch. 11 cites, does not quote.
